ui.welcome: Hello, I am SAFEx Guard. I am here to help you stay protected from scams and fraud. How can I assist you right now?
ui.triage_prompt: Please tell me what best describes your situation:

triage_options.label: I want to learn & stay safe

ui.happened_prompt: What incident occurred? Please choose below so we can take immediate protective action:
ui.learn_prompt: What security topic would you like to explore?
ui.emergency_body: Act immediately! The first 2-3 hours (Golden Hour) are crucial to block transactions and recover funds.

topics.empathy_opening: It is very wise of you to verify before clicking anything in an email.
topics.headline: Emails asking for urgent action or login credentials are often phishing attempts.
why: Scammers spoof sender display names to look like official institutions.
Malicious links lead to fake login pages designed to harvest credentials.
Attachments can contain spyware or malware that infects your smartphone.
Legitimate banks never threaten immediate account closure over email.

do_now.text: Run our quick email safety checker right now.
Inspect sender address carefully for typos (e.g. support@sbi-bank-verify.com).
Do not click any embedded link or download attachments.
Report phishing email directly to incident@cert-in.org.in.

dont: Do not click buttons like 'Update KYC Now' or 'Claim Refund'.
Do not download HTML, ZIP, or APK attachments.
Do not reply to the email with your phone number or credentials.

topics.empathy_opening: Take a deep breath. Scammers deliberately create panic so you cannot think clearly.
topics.headline: Caller creating pressure or claiming to be an official is likely a scam.
why: Fraudsters impersonate police, courier services (FedEx), telecom (TRAI), or banks.
They use voice caller-ID spoofing to look genuine.
They threaten immediate disconnection or arrest to extract money or OTPs.

do_now.text: Run our quick call analysis checklist.
Disconnect the call immediately. You owe no explanation to strangers.
Report suspicious communications on Sanchar Saathi Chakshu.
Call the official helpline if they claimed to be your bank.

dont: Do not stay on the call or switch to a video call.
Do not install any app requested by the caller (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk).
Do not read out OTP or press numbers on your keypad.

follow_up_chips.label: They claim I am under digital arrest
They asked for OTP / PIN

topics.chip_label: How to set up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
topics.empathy_opening: Securing your accounts with 2FA is the single best step to stop hackers in their tracks.
topics.headline: Two-Factor Authentication stops 99% of automated hacking attempts.
why: Even if someone steals your password, they cannot log in without the second factor.
Authenticator apps (like Google Authenticator) and passkeys are much safer than SMS OTPs.
Backup codes ensure you never get locked out of your own account.

do_now.text: Google/Gmail: Go to Google Account > Security > 2-Step Verification.
WhatsApp: Open Settings > Account > Two-Step Verification > Enable.
Social Media (Instagram/FB): Settings > Accounts Center > Password and Security > Two-factor authentication.
Bank/UPI Apps: Enable biometric login or transaction lock inside the official bank app.

dont: Never share your 2FA OTP or authenticator 6-digit code with anyone.
Do not store backup recovery codes in plain unencrypted WhatsApp notes or emails.
Menu names can change; check the app's official help page.

follow_up_chips.label: My account was already hacked
Someone asked for OTP

topics.chip_label: Someone asked for my OTP or PIN
topics.empathy_opening: Good that you stopped to check. Let's make sure your money stays safe.
topics.headline: No real bank, police or company ever needs your OTP or PIN.
why: An OTP or UPI PIN is the digital key to your money.
Scammers create artificial fear or urgency so you do not think.
Even a small '1 rupee verification' request can empty your bank account.

do_now.text: Do not share anything. End the call or stop replying immediately.
If you already shared an OTP or PIN, call 1930 immediately.
Call your bank on the official number on your card to block UPI and card.

dont: Do not read out OTP, PIN, CVV or card expiry date.
Do not click links sent by the caller on SMS or WhatsApp.
Do not install any app they suggest.

follow_up_chips.label: I already shared it and money was deducted
How do I know if a call is fake?

topics.empathy_opening: This is painful and stressful, but please know you are not alone. Let us act together right now.
topics.headline: Call 1930 immediately. Acting within the Golden Hour helps freeze stolen funds.
why: Funds hop across multiple mule bank accounts within hours.
Calling 1930 alerts the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System to freeze receiver accounts.
Immediate reporting to your bank creates a formal dispute record (RBI guidelines).

do_now.text: Call 1930 Cyber Crime Helpline right now.
Call your bank's official emergency number (on back of card) to freeze account/UPI.
Note transaction details: UTR/Transaction ID, time, debit amount, and payee handle.
File a detailed complaint on cybercrime.gov.in.
Save screenshots and SMS messages; do NOT delete any chats or call logs.

dont: Do not send additional money hoping to 'cancel' or 'reverse' the transaction.
Do not search Google for 'helpline numbers' (scammers place fake ad numbers there).
Recovery cannot be guaranteed by anyone, but fast reporting is your best chance.

follow_up_chips.label: I shared my card or Aadhaar too
My WhatsApp or email is compromised

topics.chip_label: Is this link or QR safe?
topics.empathy_opening: Stopping to inspect a link before opening or scanning is your best defense against malware.
topics.headline: Receiving money NEVER requires scanning a QR code or entering your UPI PIN.
why: QR codes only authorize outflow of money from your bank account.
Phishing links mimic banking login screens to steal passwords and OTPs.
Suspicious short links often hide direct APK downloads.

do_now.text: Never scan a QR code if someone claims they are sending you money.
Check domain letter by letter (e.g., icici-banking-login.biz is fake).
Open SAFEx URL Scanner to verify suspicious links safely.

dont: Do not scan QR codes sent on WhatsApp or OLX.
Do not open links promising lottery prizes, electricity bill waivers, or free gifts.
Do not enter UPI PIN anywhere when expecting a payment.

follow_up_chips.label: I already entered my UPI PIN
The link asked for Aadhaar/PAN

topics.chip_label: They say I am under 'Digital Arrest'
topics.empathy_opening: Please calm down. You are in safe hands. There is legally NO concept of 'Digital Arrest' in India.
topics.headline: Real Police, CBI, ED, or Customs NEVER arrest or interrogate anyone over a video call.
why: Scammers wear fake police uniforms and display fake arrest warrants on Skype/WhatsApp video calls.
They threaten that your name or Aadhaar is linked to drugs, passports, or money laundering.
They demand money transfer into 'RBI verification accounts' or 'Supreme Court escrow'—all pure fraud.

do_now.text: Disconnect the Skype or WhatsApp video call immediately.
Call the Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 immediately.
Tell your family or a trusted friend immediately; break their isolation tactic.
Report the extortion attempt on cybercrime.gov.in.

dont: Do not transfer any money to 'clear your name' or for 'security verification'.
Do not stay on camera or follow their order to stay in an isolated room.
Do not show your bank statements, passbook, or Aadhaar on video.

follow_up_chips.label: I already transferred money
They are threatening to leak my photos

topics.empathy_opening: Do not panic. Accounts can usually be recovered if we move promptly.
topics.headline: Secure recovery options immediately and terminate all unauthorized active sessions.
why: Attackers take over accounts via malware, SIM swap, or leaked credentials.
They use hacked WhatsApp/social accounts to ask your contacts for urgent money.
They change recovery emails and phone numbers to lock you out.

do_now.text: From a safe device, change your primary password immediately.
Log out of all active sessions across all devices in Security settings.
Review and update recovery email address and backup phone number.
Warn your friends and family not to send money to anyone messaging from your account.
Enable 2FA using an Authenticator app.

dont: Do not use the same compromised password across other apps or banking portals.
Do not click recovery links received via unsolicited SMS.
Do not ignore warning emails about logins from unrecognized locations.

Money was deducted from my account

topics.empathy_opening: You are not at fault, and you do not have to face this alone. Please take a deep breath.
topics.headline: Do not pay any money. Scammers will only demand more once you pay.
why: Sextortion and loan app scammers use morphed images or video call recordings to induce terror.
Paying ransom never stops extortion; it signals that the threat is effective.
Government and police have specialized cyber cells to take down non-consensual content.

do_now.text: Do NOT pay any ransom under any circumstances.
Take screenshots of chats, payment QR codes, phone numbers, and profile links.
Block the scammer on WhatsApp and social media immediately.
Call the Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or file on cybercrime.gov.in.
If you are feeling overwhelmed, call Tele-MANAS mental health helpline (14416).

dont: Do not negotiate or beg the blackmailer; it gives them leverage.
Do not delete chats before taking screenshots as evidence.
Do not blame yourself. You are the victim of a calculated crime.

follow_up_chips.label: I already paid money to them
They got my Aadhaar / contacts

topics.chip_label: I shared Aadhaar, card or personal info
topics.empathy_opening: It happens to many people. By acting right now, you can block any potential misuse.
topics.headline: Lock your biometrics on UIDAI and freeze debit/credit cards immediately.
why: Compromised card details can be used for unauthorized online or international transactions.
Aadhaar numbers paired with OTPs or biometric data can be abused for SIM issuance or loans.
Preventative locking stops unauthorized authentication requests.

do_now.text: Call your bank to block debit/credit cards and re-issue new ones.
Lock your Aadhaar biometrics via UIDAI resident portal or mAadhaar app.
Change net banking and email passwords from a secure device.
Check your CIBIL/Credit score periodically for unknown loans.

dont: Do not approve any OTP requests arriving on your phone.
Do not reuse old banking passwords.
Do not hand over physical documents to unverified representatives.

checkers.title: Email Safety Checker
checkers.intro: Answer these 6 quick questions to assess if this email is a dangerous phishing attempt.

questions.text: Does the email ask you to click a link to verify KYC, avoid account suspension, or claim a refund?
Does it create panic or an urgent deadline (e.g. 'Account blocked in 24 hours' or 'Legal action pending')?
Does it ask directly or via a link for your password, OTP, UPI PIN, Card CVV, or Aadhaar number?
Does the sender's actual email address look misspelled or end with an unusual domain (e.g., support@sbi-updates.xyz)?
Does the email contain an unexpected attachment, especially a ZIP, HTML, or APK file?
Does the email offer something too good to be true, like an unexpected lottery prize, job offer, or tax refund?

LOW_RISK.headline: Low Risk Indicators Found
LOW_RISK.body: No prominent phishing indicators were detected, but always remember that no automated checker can guarantee 100% safety. Never share passwords or OTPs.

SUSPICIOUS.headline: Suspicious Email Signs Detected
SUSPICIOUS.body: This email displays warning signs consistent with deceptive communications. Do not click any links or download attachments. Confirm directly with the sender through official channels.

LIKELY_SCAM.headline: Likely Phishing or Scam Email!
LIKELY_SCAM.body: Critical phishing indicators detected. This email is very likely an attempt to steal your credentials or money. Do NOT click anything or reply. Report to incident@cert-in.org.in.

checkers.title: Call Safety Checker
checkers.intro: Answer these 6 questions to evaluate whether this caller is a scammer impersonating an authority.

questions.text: Did the caller claim to be Police, CBI, ED, Customs, Telecom (TRAI), RBI, or Courier (FedEx)?
Did they accuse you of a crime (drugs, money laundering) or threaten immediate arrest or SIM disconnection?
Did they instruct you to stay on the call/video, keep it secret from family, or not disconnect?
Did they ask for money, OTP, UPI PIN, or to transfer money to a 'security verification account'?
Did they ask you to install an application (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk) or share your phone screen?
Did the call come from an unknown international number or an unfamiliar WhatsApp video call?

LOW_RISK.headline: No Obvious Scam Signals Detected
LOW_RISK.body: Standard precautions still apply: never share OTP, passwords, or personal details over any telephone call.

SUSPICIOUS.headline: Suspicious Call - Proceed With Caution
SUSPICIOUS.body: This caller is showing several scam patterns. Hang up and verify through the official contact number found on legitimate public websites or your bank card.

LIKELY_SCAM.headline: High Danger: Confirmed Fraud Attempt!
LIKELY_SCAM.body: This matches well-known scam operations (impersonation, digital arrest, or remote-access scam). Hang up immediately. Report on 1930 and Chakshu.

checkers.title: Link and QR Checker
checkers.intro: Follow these safety rules before opening any website link or scanning a QR code.

questions.text: Does the URL lack 'https://' or show an IP address / strange characters instead of a recognized domain name?
Does the domain imitate a reputable brand with small misspellings (e.g. sbii-online, incometax-refund-gov)?
Did someone ask you to scan a QR code to 'receive' money into your bank or UPI account?
Does the website prompt you to download and install an APK file directly onto your phone?

LOW_RISK.headline: No Immediate Red Flags
LOW_RISK.body: Proceed carefully. Always check the browser address bar to ensure you are on the legitimate domain before entering credentials.

SUSPICIOUS.headline: Questionable Link Characteristics
SUSPICIOUS.body: The link has questionable traits. Do not enter passwords, PINs, or personal data.

LIKELY_SCAM.headline: Dangerous Link or QR Scam Detected!
LIKELY_SCAM.body: High risk of malicious credential theft or malware. Do not scan the QR code and do not enter any UPI PIN.
